title: Flood and drowning
tags: flood, water rising, drowning, rescue, rain, waterlogged, flash flood
text:
1. Move to higher ground early. Never walk, swim or drive through moving water. Fast water can knock you down at ankle depth and sweep a car away at about 30 cm.
2. Switch off mains power only if it is safe and dry. Stay away from fallen cables.
3. Rescue: reach with a stick or throw a float. Do not jump in.
4. Pulled out not breathing: call 112 and start CPR; rescue breaths matter in drowning.
5. Drink only safe water. Boil or chlorinate it, and avoid floodwater (disease, snakes).

title: Earthquake
tags: earthquake, tremor, aftershock, collapse, building, trapped
text:
1. Drop, cover and hold on under a sturdy table. Stay away from windows. Do not run outside during shaking or use lifts.
2. Outdoors: move to open ground away from buildings and wires.
3. After shaking: expect aftershocks. Check for injuries and gas smell, leave damaged buildings by stairs, and do not light matches.
4. If trapped: cover your mouth, tap on a pipe or wall, use a whistle rather than shouting.

title: Cyclone and storm
tags: cyclone, storm, wind, hurricane, evacuate, shelter, warning
text:
1. Follow IMD and state warnings and evacuate early to a cyclone shelter on higher ground. Do not wait until the storm starts.
2. Take your go-bag, medicines, documents, power bank and water.
3. Stay indoors away from windows. The calm eye of a cyclone is followed by strong winds again.
4. Afterwards avoid fallen wires and floodwater.

title: Fire and smoke
tags: fire, smoke, burning, house fire, fire escape
text:
1. Alert others and leave now. Do not collect belongings. Call 101 or 112.
2. Stay low under smoke and cover your mouth with a wet cloth. Check doors with the back of your hand; do not open a hot door.
3. Close doors behind you. Never use lifts.
4. Clothes on fire: stop, drop and roll.

title: Evacuation go-bag checklist
tags: go bag, emergency kit, pack, what to carry, checklist, documents, prepare, readiness
text:
1. Water (about 3 litres per person per day), dry food, ORS.
2. Medicines for 7 days, prescriptions, inhaler or insulin.
3. ID copies, MCP or health card, emergency contacts written down.
4. Power bank, torch, whistle, charged phone, cash.
5. Sanitary pads or clean cloth, soap, spare clothes, baby supplies.
6. Glasses, hearing aids, mobility aids, spare batteries.
7. Light blanket and plastic bags. Fill in your SafeHaven profile and emergency contacts.

title: Evacuating with limited mobility, pregnancy or older age
tags: wheelchair, disability, elderly, pregnant evacuation, priority evacuation, accessible, walking difficulty, old age
text:
1. Do not wait. Ask for evacuation early and send an SOS in SafeHaven with your mobility or pregnancy flags so priority transport can be assigned.
2. Tell responders exactly what you need: wheelchair, oxygen, stairs, hearing or vision support.
3. Choose accessible shelters with ramps, accessible toilets and medical staff.
4. Pregnant: avoid long walks, carry your MCP card, and leave early in late pregnancy.
5. Agree a buddy plan with a neighbour in advance.
6. Helpers: ask before lifting. Move someone by chair carry or blanket drag only if staying is more dangerous.

title: Living in a shelter: water, sanitation and health
tags: shelter, camp, relief camp, water, sanitation, toilet, diarrhoea, hygiene, food, breastfeeding
text:
1. Drink safe water: boil for 1 minute or use chlorine tablets. Wash hands with soap before eating and after the toilet.
2. Use lit toilets in pairs and report broken locks or lights.
3. Keep food covered. For diarrhoea give ORS and fluids; get help quickly for blood in stool, high fever, very dry mouth or very little urine.
4. Pregnant, breastfeeding and new mothers can ask for priority space, food and a private corner.

title: What to tell the emergency dispatcher
tags: call 112, 108, 102, 101, 100, ambulance, dispatcher, emergency number, help line
text:
1. Call 112 (ambulance 108, maternal and child 102, fire 101, police 100, disaster helpline 1078).
2. Say where you are (landmark or GPS), what happened, how many people, and whether they are awake and breathing.
3. Mention pregnancy, allergies, medical conditions and mobility needs.
4. Stay on the line until told to hang up. Send a SafeHaven SOS to share your location; with no signal, use SMS.

title: Using SafeHaven in an emergency
tags: app, safehaven, sos, how to use, sms, offline, alert, share location, map
text:
1. Open the SOS tab, choose the emergency type, answer the questions and follow the steps shown.
2. Send the alert. Your priority level and location go to responders along with the details you chose to share.
3. No network: the alert is queued and can be sent by SMS to your emergency contact. It is delivered automatically when the connection returns.
4. The Map tab ranks shelters by medical staff and supplies. The Respond tab is for responders.
5. This assistant gives guidance only. It is not a doctor and never replaces calling 112.

title: सीपीआर और बेहोशी (CPR in Hindi)
tags: सीपीआर, बेहोश, सांस बंद, नब्ज नहीं, दिल का दौरा, होश खोना, cpr hindi, unconscious
text:
1. व्यक्ति के कंधे थपथपाएं और जोर से आवाज दें। यदि कोई जवाब न मिले तो तुरंत 112 पर कॉल करें या किसी को मदद के लिए बुलाएं।
2. सिर को पीछे झुकाएं और ठुड्डी को ऊपर उठाएं। 10 सेकंड तक देखें कि क्या सांस सामान्य रूप से चल रही है।
3. यदि सांस नहीं चल रही है: छाती के बीच में अपनी हथेली रखें और जोर से व तेजी से दबाएं (5-6 सेमी गहरा, 100-120 बार प्रति मिनट)।
4. यदि प्रशिक्षित हैं तो हर 30 बार दबाने के बाद 2 बार मुंह से सांस दें। यदि प्रशिक्षित नहीं हैं, तो बिना रुके लगातार छाती दबाते रहें।
5. जब तक एम्बुलेंस या मेडिकल सहायता न पहुंचे, सीपीआर बंद न करें।

title: गंभीर रक्तस्राव और चोट (Severe Bleeding in Hindi)
tags: खून बहना, रक्तस्राव, गहरा घाव, चोट, bleed hindi, blood loss
text:
1. तुरंत 112 पर आपातकालीन कॉल करें। यदि संभव हो तो हाथों में साफ दस्ताने या साफ प्लास्टिक बैग पहनें।
2. घाव पर साफ कपड़ा रखकर दोनों हाथों से जोर से दबाएं। दबाना बंद न करें और कपड़ा हटाकर न देखें।
3. यदि कपड़ा खून से भीग जाए, तो उसके ऊपर और कपड़ा रखें। यदि हड्डी टूटने का संदेह न हो तो अंग को दिल के स्तर से ऊपर उठाएं।
4. यदि रक्तस्राव नहीं रुक रहा है, तो घाव से 5 सेमी ऊपर चौड़ा कपड़ा या बेल्ट कसकर बांधें (टूर्निकेट) और समय नोट करें।
5. घायल को लिटाकर गर्म रखें और खाने-पीने को कुछ न दें।

title: घबराहट और पैनिक अटैक (Panic Attack in Hindi)
tags: घबराहट, पैनिक अटैक, तेज सांस, कंपन, डर, चिंता, panic hindi
text:
1. बॉक्स ब्रीदिंग (Box Breathing) कराएं: 4 सेकंड तक नाक से गहरी सांस लें, 4 सेकंड रोकें, 4 सेकंड में मुंह से धीरे-धीरे सांस छोड़ें, 4 सेकंड खाली रोकें। 5 बार दोहराएं।
2. शांत और आश्वस्त स्वर में कहें: "आप अभी पूरी तरह सुरक्षित हैं। मैं आपके साथ हूं। केवल मेरी आवाज पर ध्यान दें।"
3. 5-4-3-2-1 तकनीक: उनसे 5 चीजें देखने, 4 चीजें छूने, 3 आवाजें सुनने, 2 गंध महसूस करने को कहें।
4. टेली-मानस (Tele-MANAS) हेल्पलाइन 14416 (24 घंटे निःशुल्क) पर कॉल करें।

title: प्रसव और गर्भावस्था आपातकाल (Maternal Emergency in Hindi)
tags: प्रसव, डिलीवरी, प्रसव पीड़ा, गर्भवती, पानी की थैली फूटना, labor hindi, pregnancy
text:
1. तुरंत 112 या 102 (मातृ एवं शिशु हेल्पलाइन) पर कॉल करें। नजदीकी आशा कार्यकर्ता को सूचित करें।
2. गर्भवती को बाईं करवट (left side) पर लिटाएं। उन्हें शांत रखें।
3. यदि संकुचन (contractions) हर 2-3 मिनट में हो रहे हैं या शिशु का सिर दिखने लगे, तो यात्रा न करें। साफ चादर बिछाएं।
4. शिशु का सिर बाहर आने पर उसे हल्के से सहारा दें, कभी भी खींचे नहीं।
5. जन्म के तुरंत बाद शिशु को साफ सूखे कपड़े से पोंछें, मां की छाती पर त्वचा से त्वचा सटाकर (skin-to-skin) लिटाएं और दोनों को गर्म रखें।
6. गर्भनाल (umbilical cord) को कभी न काटें; स्वास्थ्य कार्यकर्ता के आने की प्रतीक्षा करें।

title: Labour and imminent childbirth
tags: labour, labor, delivery, childbirth, giving birth, contractions, water broke, baby coming, crowning, pushing
text:
1. Call 112 or 102 and a health worker or ASHA. Go to the nearest facility only if you can travel safely.
2. Birth is near if contractions are 2 to 3 minutes apart, she feels the urge to push, or the baby's head is visible. Then do not travel.
3. Help her lie semi-sitting or on her left side on clean cloths. Wash your hands. Let the baby come out by itself and support the head gently. Never pull.
4. If the cord is loose around the neck, slip it over the head. Do not pull the cord.
5. After birth: dry the baby, wrap warm, place skin to skin on the mother's chest and cover both and the baby's head. Note the time.
6. Do not cut the cord; wait for responders. Let the placenta come out by itself and keep it with the baby.
7. Encourage breastfeeding and gently massage her lower belly. Heavy bleeding needs urgent help.
Call 112 if: always.

title: Danger signs in pregnancy
tags: pregnant, pregnancy, eclampsia, preeclampsia, bleeding, headache, blurred vision, reduced movement, water leaking, fever, swelling
text:
Call 112 or 102 or go to the nearest facility at once for any of these:
1. Vaginal bleeding.
2. Fits or convulsions.
3. Severe headache with blurred vision, or sudden swelling of face and hands.
4. Severe belly pain.
5. Fluid leaking, or labour starting before 37 weeks.
6. Baby moving much less or not at all.
7. Fever with chills.
8. Difficulty breathing or chest pain.
9. Vomiting so much she cannot keep fluids down.
While waiting, lie on the left side. Take the MCP card and medicines.

title: Heavy bleeding after childbirth
tags: postpartum haemorrhage, pph, bleeding after delivery, placenta, after birth
text:
1. Call 112 or 102 now. Lay her flat, legs raised, and keep her warm.
2. Massage the lower belly firmly in circles until it feels hard like a ball. Keep massaging.
3. Put the baby to the breast; suckling helps the womb contract.
4. Help her pass urine if she can. Press a clean pad on any visible tear.
5. Give nothing by mouth if she is faint or drowsy.

title: Bleeding or pain in early pregnancy
tags: miscarriage, spotting, early pregnancy, ectopic, cramps, bleeding
text:
1. Light spotting: rest and see a doctor the same day.
2. Heavy bleeding (soaking a pad in an hour), strong one-sided belly pain, shoulder pain, dizziness or fainting: call 112. It may be an ectopic pregnancy or miscarriage.
3. Put nothing in the vagina. Keep any tissue passed to show the doctor.

title: Newborn care in emergencies
tags: newborn, baby, infant, breastfeeding, warm, cord, fever baby
text:
1. Keep the baby warm: skin to skin, head covered, wrapped; never leave on a cold floor.
2. Breastfeed soon after birth and often. Wash hands first. Give no water, honey or other fluids.
3. Danger signs: not feeding, fast or difficult breathing, fever or very cold, fits, floppy, blue lips, yellow skin in the first 24 hours. Get urgent care or call 108.
4. Keep the cord stump clean and dry.

title: Periods and menstrual hygiene in emergencies
tags: sanitary pad, menstrual, period, hygiene, shelter, cloth, privacy, menstruation
text:
1. Ask shelter staff or volunteers for pads and for female volunteers. You have a right to privacy and dignity.
2. No pads: use several layers of clean cotton cloth. Change every 4 to 6 hours, wash with soap and clean water, dry fully in sun or air, store clean. Never share cloths.
3. Wrap used pads in a bag and put them in the bin. Wash hands after.
4. Soaking a pad every hour for several hours, fever or foul smell: see a health worker.
5. The SafeHaven Map tab shows which shelters have hygiene kits in stock.

title: Medicines and chronic conditions during evacuation
tags: medicine, medication, insulin, chronic, diabetes, bp, hypertension, thyroid, epilepsy, tablets, prescription
text:
1. Carry at least 7 days of regular medicines in original packs with the prescription or a photo of it.
2. Insulin: keep cool and never frozen, for example in a wet cloth or insulated bag.
3. Do not stop treatment for diabetes, blood pressure, epilepsy, TB, HIV or heart disease. Tell the shelter health team what you take.
4. Keep inhaler, auto-injector, spare glasses, hearing aid batteries and mobility aids with you.
5. Complete your SafeHaven profile so responders know what you need.

title: Mental health: panic and distress
tags: want to die, suicide, self harm, hopeless, panic, anxiety, fear, trauma, grief, overwhelmed, stress, cannot calm down, crying
text:
1. Slow your breathing: in for 4 counts, out for 6, repeat for a few minutes.
2. Ground yourself: name 5 things you see, 4 you can touch, 3 you hear.
3. Stay near someone you trust. Drink water, eat something, rest when you can.
4. Tele-MANAS 14416 is a free 24/7 mental health helpline. If you think of harming yourself, call 112 or 14416 now and stay with someone.

title: Safety, harassment and violence against women
tags: women safety, harassment, assault, abuse, violence, unsafe, helpline, 181, 1091, rape, threat
text:
1. If you are in danger, call 112. Women's helpline 181; police women's helpline 1091; child helpline 1098.
2. In shelters, ask for a place near other women and families in a lit area. Go to toilets in pairs. Tell the coordinator or police about any threat.
3. Keep your phone charged and send a SafeHaven SOS to share your live location.
4. After a sexual assault: go to a safe place, seek medical care (emergency treatment is available), and know it is not your fault. Do not wash or change clothes if you may want to report.

title: Not breathing or unresponsive (CPR)
tags: cpr, unconscious, collapsed, no pulse, not breathing, cardiac arrest, unresponsive, heart stopped, not waking
text:
1. Check the scene is safe. Shout and tap the shoulders. No response: shout for help, call 112 and send someone for an AED.
2. Tilt the head back and lift the chin. Look for normal breathing for no more than 10 seconds. Gasping is not normal breathing.
3. Not breathing normally: push hard and fast on the centre of the chest, about 5-6 cm deep, 100-120 times a minute. Let the chest rise fully between pushes.
4. If trained, give 2 rescue breaths after every 30 compressions. If not, keep doing compressions only.
5. Use an AED as soon as it arrives and follow its voice prompts. Do not stop until help takes over or the person breathes normally.
6. Late pregnancy: start CPR at once. With a second helper, gently push the belly toward her left side.
Call 112 if: always.

title: Severe bleeding
tags: heavy bleeding, blood loss, wound, cut, haemorrhage, bleeding won't stop, injury
text:
1. Call 112. Use gloves or a clean plastic bag on your hands if possible.
2. Press firmly on the wound with a clean cloth. Keep pressing; do not lift to check.
3. If blood soaks through, add more cloth on top. Raise the limb if a fracture is not suspected.
4. Bandage firmly once bleeding slows. Only if a limb is bleeding dangerously and pressure fails, tie a wide strip tightly above the wound and note the time.
5. Lay the person down, keep them warm, give nothing to eat or drink. Do not pull out objects stuck in a wound; press around them.

title: Choking
tags: choke, cannot breathe, food stuck, airway blocked, swallowed
text:
1. If they can cough or speak, encourage coughing and stay close.
2. If they cannot breathe, speak or cough: lean them forward and give up to 5 firm back blows between the shoulder blades.
3. Then up to 5 abdominal thrusts: fist above the navel, pull sharply inward and upward. In late pregnancy or for a very large person, give chest thrusts at the centre of the chest instead.
4. Alternate back blows and thrusts. Call 112 if it does not clear. If they become unresponsive, start CPR.
5. Infant under 1 year: 5 back blows with the head lower than the body along your forearm, then 5 chest thrusts with two fingers. No abdominal thrusts.

title: Chest pain or suspected heart attack
tags: heart attack, chest pressure, tight chest, pain in left arm, jaw pain, sweating, breathless, angina
text:
1. Call 112. Stop all activity and sit the person half upright with knees bent.
2. Loosen tight clothing and keep them calm. Do not let them walk or drive.
3. If they are not allergic and a doctor has not told them to avoid it, they may chew one 300 mg aspirin.
4. Women often have less typical signs: breathlessness, nausea, back or jaw pain, unusual tiredness. Take them seriously.
5. If they stop responding and are not breathing normally, start CPR.

title: Stroke
tags: stroke, face drooping, slurred speech, arm weakness, sudden numbness, confusion, brain attack
text:
1. Think FAST: Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech slurred, Time to call 112.
2. Note the time the symptoms started and tell the responders.
3. Keep them sitting or lying with the head slightly raised. Give nothing to eat or drink and no aspirin.
4. Sudden severe headache, loss of vision or confusion also need urgent care.

title: Seizure or fits
tags: seizure, convulsion, fit, epilepsy, shaking, eclampsia
text:
1. Note the time. Clear hard objects away and cushion the head.
2. Do not hold them down or put anything in their mouth.
3. When the shaking stops, turn them onto their side and check breathing. Stay until they are fully awake.
4. Call 112 if it lasts more than 5 minutes, repeats, it is their first seizure, they are injured, or they are pregnant.

title: Burns
tags: burn, scald, fire injury, hot oil, hot water, blister
text:
1. Move away from the heat. Remove rings and loose clothing near the burn unless stuck to the skin.
2. Cool with clean running water for 20 minutes. No ice, butter, toothpaste or oil.
3. Cover loosely with cling film or a clean non-fluffy cloth. Do not burst blisters.
4. Go to hospital or call 112 for burns larger than the person's palm, on the face, hands, genitals or joints, deep, chemical or electrical burns, or in children and older people.
5. Clothes on fire: stop, drop and roll.

title: Fracture or injury
tags: fracture, broken bone, sprain, swelling, fall, spine injury, neck injury
text:
1. Do not move them unless in danger. Keep the injured part still.
2. Do not straighten the limb. Support it as found with rolled clothes or a padded splint covering the joints above and below.
3. Suspected neck or back injury: keep head and body still and call 112.
4. If fingers or toes turn pale, blue or numb, loosen the wrap. A cold pack wrapped in cloth reduces swelling.

title: Fainting or dizziness
tags: faint, dizzy, blackout, light headed, collapse
text:
1. Lay the person flat and raise the legs about 30 cm. Loosen tight clothing and give fresh air.
2. If pregnant, lay her on her left side instead of flat on her back.
3. When awake and able to swallow, give sips of water or something sweet.
4. Call 112 if they do not wake within a minute, are injured, have chest pain, or are pregnant with bleeding or severe pain.

title: Heat exhaustion and heatstroke
tags: heatwave, sunstroke, hot, dehydration, confusion, hot dry skin, extreme heat
text:
1. Move to shade or a cool room. Remove extra clothing.
2. Cool quickly: wet the skin, fan, and place cold packs on the neck, armpits and groin.
3. If awake, give small sips of cool water or ORS.
4. Confusion, fits, fainting or hot dry skin means heatstroke: call 112 and keep cooling until help arrives.
5. Pregnant women, older people and children overheat faster.

title: Low blood sugar (diabetes)
tags: diabetes, hypoglycaemia, low sugar, shaky, sweating, insulin
text:
1. Signs: shaking, sweating, hunger, confusion, irritability.
2. If awake and able to swallow, give about 15 g of fast sugar, such as 3 teaspoons of sugar in water or a glass of juice. Recheck after 15 minutes, repeat if still low, then give a snack.
3. If unconscious or unable to swallow, put nothing in the mouth, place them on their side and call 112.

title: Asthma or severe breathlessness
tags: asthma, wheeze, short of breath, inhaler, difficulty breathing, breathless
text:
1. Sit upright and stay calm. Loosen clothing and move away from smoke or dust.
2. Use the reliever inhaler (usually blue) as prescribed, with a spacer if available.
3. If there is no improvement, lips turn blue, or they cannot speak in full sentences, call 112 and keep using the reliever as prescribed.

title: Severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis)
tags: allergy, anaphylaxis, swelling throat, hives, sting, adrenaline, epipen, food allergy
text:
1. Signs: swelling of lips, face or throat, wheeze, trouble breathing, widespread hives or dizziness after a sting, food or medicine.
2. Call 112. If they have an adrenaline auto-injector, use it at once on the outer thigh and note the time.
3. Lay them flat with legs raised. If breathing is hard, let them sit up. Do not stand them up suddenly.
4. If there is no improvement after 5 to 15 minutes and a second auto-injector is available, use it.

title: Snake or animal bite
tags: snake, snakebite, dog bite, rabies, venom, animal bite
text:
1. Move away. Do not catch or kill the animal. Keep the person calm and still.
2. Keep the bitten limb at heart level and remove rings. Wrap loosely and immobilise with a splint.
3. Do not cut, suck, burn or tie tight bands. Do not give alcohol.
4. Go to a hospital with antivenom or rabies treatment at once and call 108 or 112.
5. Dog or animal bite: wash with soap and running water for 15 minutes and seek rabies vaccination.

title: Poisoning or swallowed chemicals
tags: poison, swallowed, chemical, overdose, pesticide, kerosene
text:
1. Call 112 and follow their instructions. Keep the container or label to show the doctor.
2. Do not make the person vomit. Remove contaminated clothing.
3. Chemical on skin or eyes: rinse with running water for 15 to 20 minutes.
4. If unconscious, place on their side and check breathing.

title: Electric shock
tags: electric shock, electrocution, fallen wire, live wire, current
text:
1. Do not touch the person until the power is off or you have moved the source away with dry wood or plastic.
2. Call 112. If they are not breathing normally, start CPR. Cover burns loosely.
3. Everyone who has had an electric shock should be checked at a hospital. Stay away from fallen wires, especially in floods and storms.

title: Panic attack, extreme anxiety and shock
tags: panic attack, anxiety, hyperventilating, rapid breathing, shaking, fear, terrified, trauma, crying, panic, mental health
text:
1. Guide their breathing with Box Breathing: Inhale slowly through the nose for 4 seconds, hold for 4 seconds, exhale slowly through the mouth for 4 seconds, hold for 4 seconds. Repeat 5 times.
2. Speak in a calm, low, firm voice: "You are safe right now. I am here with you. Focus on my voice."
3. Use the 5-4-3-2-1 Grounding method: Ask them to name 5 things they see, 4 things they can feel, 3 things they can hear, 2 things they can smell, and 1 positive affirmation.
4. If hyperventilating (breathing very fast): Have them cup their hands loosely around mouth and nose or breathe with pursed lips. Do not use a paper bag if heart or lung disease is possible.
5. Keep them warm with a blanket or jacket. Shock often causes shivering and feeling cold.
6. For severe acute mental distress or suicidal thoughts in India, call Tele-MANAS at 14416 (24/7 free) or 112.

title: Psychological first aid in disaster
tags: shock, psychological first aid, trauma, grief, overwhelmed, disaster stress, scared children
text:
1. Look: Ensure immediate safety, check for physical injuries, and protect from further trauma or sight of severe casualties.
2. Listen: Approach calmly, introduce yourself, ask what they need most, and listen without interrupting or giving false promises.
3. Link: Connect families together, provide clean drinking water, food, and private shelter.
4. For children: Speak at eye level, keep them close to trusted family, give simple honest facts, and provide comfort items.

title: Emergency supply substitutes and field alternatives
tags: supply alternative, out of stock, substitute, no water, no medicine, or substitute, emergency rations, makeshift dressing, clean water
text:
1. Safe drinking water without tablets: Boil water vigorously for at least 1 full minute (3 minutes at high altitude). Let it cool naturally. If boiling is impossible, filter murky water through multiple layers of clean cotton cloth, then use household unscented bleach (2 drops of 6% sodium hypochlorite per 1 litre of clear water; wait 30 minutes before drinking).
2. Homemade Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) substitute: Mix 6 level teaspoons of sugar and 1/2 level teaspoon of salt into 1 litre of clean boiled water. Stir until dissolved. Taste should be no saltier than tears. Give frequent small sips.
3. Sterile wound dressings and gauze: Use clean, unused cotton cloth, t-shirts, or handkerchiefs. If unsterile, iron the cloth with high heat on both sides or scorch briefly over clean heat to kill surface pathogens before applying.
4. Makeshift splints for limb fractures: Use rolled newspapers, magazines, flat wooden rulers, straight tree branches, or cardboard. Pad with towels or cloth and tie firmly above and below the fracture using strips of cloth. Never tie directly over the fracture.
5. Improvised emergency warmth / hypothermia: Layer dry newspapers between clothing for insulation. Wrap person in a large plastic bag or garbage bag with head hole to stop evaporative cooling and wind chill.
6. Sanitary pads and maternal hygiene alternative: Layer clean, soft cotton cloths. Change every 4 to 6 hours. Wash thoroughly with clean water and soap, dry in direct sunlight. Never use unwashed rags, leaves, or dirty plastic against sensitive skin.
7. Baby formula shortage: Exclusively breastfeed if possible (even mothers under stress produce protective milk). For non-breastfed infants over 6 months in acute emergency, clean boiled animal milk diluted with clean boiled water (3 parts milk to 1 part water) with a tiny pinch of sugar can provide short-term survival calories until relief supplies arrive.
